events.title: Mary Shelley, Author of Frankenstein, Is Born
events.description: Mary Wollstonecraft Godwin was born in London to the philosopher William Godwin and the pioneering feminist Mary Wollstonecraft. As Mary Shelley, she went on to write Frankenstein, one of the most influential novels in English.
events.significance: Her 1818 novel helped launch science fiction and still shapes how we talk about science, ambition and responsibility.

events.title: Melbourne Is Founded
events.description: Settlers from Van Diemen's Land (now Tasmania) established a settlement on the Yarra River, in what is now Australia's second-largest city. The city of Melbourne grew from this beginning.
events.significance: The settlement grew into a major cultural and economic centre of Australia, and it was one of the world's great boomtowns during the 1850s gold rush.

events.title: Ernest Rutherford, Father of Nuclear Physics, Is Born
events.description: Ernest Rutherford was born in Spring Grove, New Zealand. He became one of the most influential experimental physicists in history and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
events.significance: His work revealed the structure of the atom, including the nucleus, and laid the foundations of modern nuclear physics.

events.title: Lenin Wounded and Uritsky Killed in Assassination Attacks
events.description: On the same day in Soviet Russia, Bolshevik leader Vladimir Lenin was seriously wounded in a shooting in Moscow, and the senior Bolshevik official Moisei Uritsky was killed in Petrograd.
events.significance: The attacks were used to justify the Red Terror, a brutal campaign of repression during the Russian Civil War.

events.title: Hong Kong Is Liberated from Japanese Occupation
events.description: At the end of World War II, British forces arrived in Hong Kong, ending nearly four years of Japanese occupation.
events.significance: It marked the return of the territory to British administration and the start of its postwar recovery.
